subject.title: codex harness chat.send image turn completes with no assistant reply (live, api-key route)

question: Should this be treated as an OpenClaw attachment/projection regression now, or should the lane first require a route-and-model comparison proving that `openai/gpt-5.6-luna` can read the bitmap through direct Codex app-server input?
rationale: The live failure is credible and user-visible, but the available evidence cannot yet allocate ownership between OpenClaw serialization, Codex event projection, and model capability; choosing the proof threshold affects both the implementation boundary and whether the maintained lane should change.

options.title: Instrument both paths first
options.body: Capture and compare `turn/start` inputs, Codex item events, terminal outcomes, and session history for the passing `agent` probe and failing `chat.send` probe before selecting the fix owner.

options.title: Treat as OpenClaw regression
options.body: Assume the maintained API-key lane defines the contract and immediately debug the gateway attachment and assistant-projection paths without requiring a second model comparison.

options.title: Adjust the live lane
options.body: Use a different supported model or weaken the OCR assertion only if direct app-server proof shows the current model or route cannot satisfy the existing bitmap-read expectation.

recommendation.title: Instrument both paths first
recommendation.body: Capture and compare `turn/start` inputs, Codex item events, terminal outcomes, and session history for the passing `agent` probe and failing `chat.send` probe before selecting the fix owner.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history connects this person most directly to the managed Codex runtime, model compatibility, and live harness diagnostics needed to make this proof decision.
